html:
A Brazilian rubber tapper, union leader and environmentalist from Acre in the western Amazon, who fought to protect the Amazon rainforest and the people who lived from it. He was murdered in 1988.

He grew up tapping wild rubber like his father, whose family came to the forest in the wake of the rubber boom. In the 1970s ranchers moved into Acre, clearing forest for cattle pastures, often with violence. Mendes led the tappers' union in "empates", standoffs in which families stood peacefully in front of the chainsaw crews.

He argued that the forest could be used without being destroyed, and proposed "extractive reserves", protected areas where local people could harvest rubber, nuts and other products. He won international attention and prizes. On 22 December 1988 he was shot dead at his home by a rancher's son. The outcry led Brazil to create the first extractive reserves, including one named after him. Like the Trans-Amazonian Highway, his story marks the fight over the Amazon's future.
sum: A Brazilian rubber tapper, union leader and environmentalist from Acre in the western Amazon, who fought to protect the Amazon rainforest and the people who lived from it. He was murdered in 1988.
